about: Differences scripts/schema_parity.py accepts between the schema pantry-db's migrations build (mig) and the one pantry-api's models build with create_all (orm).
Each line is one difference exactly as the script prints it; each group says why its lines are acceptable. A difference not listed here fails the schema-parity job.

The 0001-0006 entries record what the job found when it was added. A line for a table the pinned checkouts do not have yet (origin_submissions arrives with 0006, recipe_line_amounts with 0007) is reported as not found and does not fail.

allowed.reason: run-migrations.sh creates schema_migrations to record which migrations it has applied. It is the runner's own bookkeeping; pantry-api never reads it, so no model declares it.
diffs: table schema_migrations: only in mig

allowed.reason: The migrations declare these primary keys as plain integers, and SQLAlchemy builds a lone Integer primary key as SERIAL, so create_all adds a sequence default. Every one of these rows is written with its id: products, stores and reviews by the seed (seed.sql, or db.seed_from_json in pantry-api), product_origins under the product it describes. The sequence is never used.
diffs: column product_origins.product_id: default mig none, orm serial
column products.id: default mig none, orm serial
column reviews.id: default mig none, orm serial
column stores.id: default mig none, orm serial

allowed.reason: The migrations use integer GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY and the models autoincrement=True, which create_all builds as SERIAL. Both number a row whose insert leaves the id out and accept an explicit id, which is all pantry-api relies on.
diffs: column origin_submissions.id: default mig identity, orm serial
column price_observations.id: default mig identity, orm serial
column product_origin_evidence.id: default mig identity, orm serial

allowed.reason: The models give these columns a Python-side default= and no server_default, so create_all writes no DEFAULT where the migration has one. Rows written through the models always carry the value, so pantry-api behaves the same on either schema; only seed.sql and hand-written SQL rely on the SQL default. A new model column declares server_default to match its migration, as RecipeLineAmountRow does for 0007.

allowed.reason: 0002 added products.unit_qty as REAL, a 4-byte float, while the model's Float builds double precision, so pantry-api's Postgres tests run on a wider column than production. Every seeded unit_qty is a whole number no larger than 4540, which REAL stores exactly; a fractional size such as 2.2 would read back slightly different in production only. Widening the column is left to a later, separately reviewed migration.
diffs: column products.unit_qty: type mig real, orm double precision

allowed.reason: pantry-api's models declare no foreign keys: by convention each one lives in the migrations only (RecipeLineAmountRow's docstring in db.py says so). Production enforces them; pantry-api's test databases do not. A foreign key that a model declares and the migrations lack is not listed here, so it would fail.

allowed.reason: The models declare no CHECK constraints; these live in the migrations only. Production rejects a value outside them; pantry-api's test databases accept it.
